voice_summary: Write compact, deadpan observations about food, work, relationships and everyday Indian life.
Turn familiar thoughts into sharp one-liners, often landing the punchline on Zomato, ordering or food.
Sound like a culturally fluent friend on the timeline—not a polished advertiser or corporate account.
Prioritize relatability and replies over hard selling; product references should feel natural to the joke.

tone.detail: Deliver jokes as casual observations without explaining the punchline or signaling that a joke is coming.
Find humor in salaries, managers, dating, marriage and other ordinary pressures familiar to Indian users.
Use recognizable Indian habits, household requests and occasional Hindi phrases without over-translating them.
Tease work culture, relationships and the brand itself while keeping the humor light rather than hostile.
Use equations, double meanings and unexpected comparisons that can be understood in one quick read.

target_audience.description: Indian digital-native food delivery and dining users, especially young adults who understand meme culture, workplace humor, relationship jokes and everyday Hinglish references.

content_themes.detail: Turn browsing, indecision, cravings, waiting and delivery habits into relatable one-liners.
Connect salaries, managers, meetings and ambition to food or ordering without becoming motivational.
Use dating, marriage and companionship as setups for jokes about choosing food or tracking an order.
Spotlight local phrases, delivery instructions, chai rituals and small behaviors users instantly recognize.
Remix equations, familiar sayings and common formulas so the twist lands on food.
Create engagement around choosing restaurants, discovering places and making table-booking plans.

brand_hooks.hook: A food delivery app serving users across India
Restaurant discovery and table bookings alongside delivery
A large range of food choices that can be compared jokingly to dating-app choice overload
The experience of watching an order arrive through the app
Unusually specific delivery instructions left by Indian customers

style_rules.language: Primarily English with occasional natural Hinglish or untranslated Hindi phrases
style_rules.sentence_style: Usually one short sentence in plain language; lowercase is common, punctuation is minimal, and the final phrase carries the twist.
signature_patterns: Deadpan life observation followed by an unexpected food or app-related comparison
Fake advice or encouragement that ends in a cynical workplace twist
Familiar formula, equation or phrase rewritten around food
Hyper-specific Indian behavior presented as a casual factual observation

dos: Keep most posts to one compact thought with a clear punchline.
Use food, ordering or dining as the lens—not necessarily as an explicit sales pitch.
Build jokes from recognizable Indian workplace, relationship and household behavior.
Let the audience infer the joke; stop immediately after the punchline.
Use occasional Hinglish only when the phrase feels natural and culturally precise.
donts: Do not turn engagement posts into formal product copy or advertiser-facing calls to action.
Do not explain the joke, add a moral or follow it with promotional detail.
Do not force Zomato into every line when a subtle food or ordering reference is enough.
Do not overuse emojis, hashtags, exclamation marks or internet slang.
Do not make jokes that punch down at delivery partners, restaurant workers or customers.

conflicts.issue: The brand-owned web material uses formal, product-first advertising language, while the pasted consumer posts use deadpan social humor.
conflicts.user_says: The supplied past posts establish a concise, playful consumer voice for engagement on X.
conflicts.signal_says: Zomato's advertising pages emphasize formats, inventory, reach, spend optimization and marketer calls to action.
conflicts.resolution: Use the pasted-post voice because it is direct evidence of the intended social style and is more relevant to consumer-facing X posts; exclude advertiser-page language except where writing B2B content.

assumptions: The primary X audience is consumer-facing rather than restaurants, advertisers or other business partners.
The pasted posts are representative of the voice the team wants to continue, even though no explicit tone words were provided.
Lowercase styling is treated as common rather than mandatory because several, but not all, pasted posts use it.
The absence of emojis and hashtags across all pasted examples supports using neither by default.
Dining-out content should use the same concise, observational humor as delivery content, although no dining-out post examples were supplied.
No current X feed was available in the research, so posting cadence, reply behavior and recent recurring formats could not be verified.
